city and the stars.title: The City and the Stars
city and the stars.author: Arthur C. Clarke
city and the stars.why: Clarke's far-future tale of a perfect city and a young man who wants to leave it; a classic of old science fiction.

hunter.title: The Hunter
hunter.author: Tana French
hunter.why: Comments are lukewarm about it or about a neighbouring book; not a clear recommendation.

sense of an ending.title: The Sense of an Ending
sense of an ending.author: Julian Barnes
sense of an ending.why: A retired man's memory of his youth is overturned by a late discovery; a short novel readers call mind-blowing.

beggars in spain.title: Beggars in Spain
beggars in spain.author: Nancy Kress
beggars in spain.why: Genetically engineered people who never sleep split society in this thoughtful near-future novel, with sequels.

wise blood.title: Wise blood
wise blood.author: Flannery O'Connor
wise blood.why: O'Connor's Southern Gothic about a man founding a church without Christ; strange, dark and sharply comic.

dead souls.title: Dead Souls
dead souls.author: Nikolaĭ Vasilʹevich  Gogolʹ
dead souls.why: Gogol's satire of a con man buying dead serfs; readers say it intrigues and entertains them.

bright young women.title: Bright Young Women
bright young women.author: Jessica Knoll
bright young women.why: A fictional take on the Ted Bundy crimes told from the women's side; a recommended true-crime-style thriller.

snow flower and the secret fan.title: Snow Flower and the Secret Fan
snow flower and the secret fan.author: Lisa See
snow flower and the secret fan.why: Two girls in 19th-century China are bound as lifelong friends through a secret women's script; widely loved.

civil campaign.title: A Civil Campaign
civil campaign.author: Lois McMaster Bujold
civil campaign.why: A comedy of manners in the Vorkosigan saga, mixing romance, politics and disaster dinners; a high point for fans.

liars club.title: The Liars' Club
liars club.author: Mary Karr
liars club.why: Mary Karr's memoir of a chaotic Texas childhood with sharp humour; readers call it wonderful.

early riser.title: Early Riser
early riser.author: Jasper Fforde
early riser.why: A winter-sleeping world is full of dreams and danger; very British humour that readers found damn funny.

choke.title: Choke
choke.author: Chuck Palahniuk
choke.why: One reader is neutral and the other only describes the plot; not clearly recommended.

instructions.title: The Instructions
instructions.author: Adam Levin
instructions.why: A huge, wild novel about a ten-year-old self-proclaimed messiah at a Chicago school; ambitious and divisive.

fifteen dogs.title: Fifteen Dogs
fifteen dogs.author: André Alexis
fifteen dogs.why: Two gods give dogs human intelligence and watch what happens; readers call it a unique, moving fable.

incidents around the house.title: Incidents Around the House
incidents around the house.author: Josh Malerman
incidents around the house.why: One reader calls it a bad, mediocre book; it is not recommended.

wonder.title: Wonder
wonder.author: R. J. Palacio
wonder.why: Mentions are tied to lists about other books, and the Palacio novel is not clearly recommended.

witching hour.title: The Witching Hour
witching hour.author: Anne Rice
witching hour.why: A doctor learns of the Mayfair family of witches in a vast Gothic saga; a good pick for Anne Rice fans.

vineland.title: Vineland
vineland.author: Thomas Pynchon
vineland.why: Pynchon's loosely plotted tale of a hippie-era family in California under Reagan; suggested as an easier way into him.

in the garden of beasts.title: In the garden of beasts
in the garden of beasts.author: Erik Larson
in the garden of beasts.why: The US ambassador and his family in 1930s Berlin as Hitler rises; Larson's story reads like a thriller.

conspiracy against the human race.title: The Conspiracy Against the Human Race
conspiracy against the human race.author: Thomas Ligotti
conspiracy against the human race.why: Ligotti's bleak philosophical case that consciousness is a curse; for readers who like their pessimism uncompromising.

namesake.title: The Namesake
namesake.author: Jhumpa Lahiri
namesake.why: An Indian-American family across generations deals with names, tradition and loss; a quietly affecting novel.

girl who drank the moon.title: The Girl Who Drank the Moon
girl who drank the moon.author: Kelly Regan Barnhill
girl who drank the moon.why: A good witch accidentally gives a baby magic; a fairytale a child asked a parent to read.

nix.title: The Nix
nix.author: Nathan Hill
nix.why: A professor and his estranged mother's past connect in a funny, sprawling novel that readers couldn't put down.

duma key.title: Duma Key
duma key.author: Stephen King
duma key.why: An injured man paints terrifying things in a Florida island house; a King favourite, also great on audiobook.

pnin.title: Pnin
pnin.author: Vladimir Nabokov
pnin.why: Nabokov's gentle, comic story of a Russian professor at an American college; readers return to it.

vera wongs unsolicited advice for murder.title: Vera Wong's Unsolicited Advice for Murderers
vera wongs unsolicited advice for murder.author: Jesse Q. Sutanto
vera wongs unsolicited advice for murder.why: A busybody tea shop owner turns detective when a body appears in her shop; a lighthearted cosy mystery.

red sister.title: Red Sister
red sister.author: Mark Lawrence
red sister.why: A young killer is trained at a convent of fighting nuns in a gritty world; a memorable opening line.

girl who loved tom gordon.title: The Girl Who Loved Tom Gordon
girl who loved tom gordon.author: Stephen King
girl who loved tom gordon.why: A nine-year-old lost in the woods clings to baseball; a short King that readers say hooked them on his work.

great circle.title: Great Circle
great circle.author: Maggie Shipstead
great circle.why: A female pilot's life and the actress who plays her decades later are intertwined; the story stayed with readers.

southern book clubs guide to slaying vam.title: The Southern Book Club's Guide to Slaying Vampires
southern book clubs guide to slaying vam.author: Grady Hendrix
southern book clubs guide to slaying vam.why: Women in a book club in South Carolina discover a vampire next door; a fun, gory horror comedy.

psalm for the wild built.title: A Psalm for the Wild-Built
psalm for the wild built.author: Becky Chambers
psalm for the wild built.why: A tea monk and a robot talk about what people need; a short, comforting book called one of the best.

illusions.title: Illusions: The Adventures of a Reluctant Messiah
illusions.author: Richard Bach
illusions.why: A pilot meets a messiah who teaches simple, hopeful lessons; readers re-read it as a comforting guide.

mockingbird.title: Mockingbird
mockingbird.author: Walter S. Tevis
mockingbird.why: The comments refer to Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird rather than this Tevis novel.

hidden pictures.title: Hidden Pictures
hidden pictures.author: Jason Rekulak
hidden pictures.why: A babysitter finds disturbing drawings by her charge; a quick ghost story and thriller.

bridge to terabithia.title: Bridge to Terabithia
bridge to terabithia.author: Katherine Paterson
bridge to terabithia.why: Two friends invent a magical kingdom in the woods and then face loss; a favourite childhood tearjerker.

adventures of amina al sirafi.title: The Adventures of Amina Al-Sirafi
adventures of amina al sirafi.author: Shannon A. Chakraborty
adventures of amina al sirafi.why: A retired pirate captain takes one last job in the medieval Indian Ocean; praised as a lively pirate adventure.

worst hard time.title: The worst hard time
worst hard time.author: Timothy Egan
worst hard time.why: The Dust Bowl told through the people who stayed on the Plains; recommended for fans of narrative history.

best served cold.title: Best served cold
best served cold.author: Joe Abercrombie
best served cold.why: A mercenary seeks bloody revenge in Abercrombie's grim fantasy; a fast standalone that readers love.

monstrous regiment.title: Monstrous Regiment
monstrous regiment.author: Terry Pratchett
monstrous regiment.why: A girl disguises herself as a boy to join the army in a Discworld satire of war and gender.

river of doubt.title: The River of Doubt
river of doubt.author: Candice Millard
river of doubt.why: Theodore Roosevelt's near-fatal expedition down an unmapped Amazon river; an epic, harrowing true story.

shadow divers.title: Shadow Divers
shadow divers.author: Robert Kurson
shadow divers.why: Two divers find a sunken U-boat off New Jersey and try to identify it; great for wreck-diving fans.

tehanu.title: Tehanu (The Earthsea Cycle, Book 4)
tehanu.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
tehanu.why: The comments discuss other Earthsea books and the other works; this title is not clearly recommended.

eat pray love.title: Eat, Pray, Love
eat pray love.author: Elizabeth Gilbert
eat pray love.why: Readers call it overrated or say they hated it; not recommended.

dolores claiborne.title: Dolores Claiborne
dolores claiborne.author: Stephen King
dolores claiborne.why: A woman recounts her life and a murder to police in a monologue; a short, tough King novel.

bobiverse.title: We Are Legion (We Are Bob)
bobiverse.author: Dennis E. Taylor
bobiverse.why: A software engineer's mind becomes a self-replicating space probe; a funny, popular first book in the Bobiverse series.

book lovers.title: Book Lovers
book lovers.author: Emily Henry
book lovers.why: A literary agent and an editor keep meeting in a small town; an easy, enjoyable romance even for non-fans.

circle.title: The Circle
circle.author: Dave Eggers
circle.why: A young woman joins a tech giant that demands complete transparency; a gripping near-future cautionary tale.

eifelheim.title: Eifelheim
eifelheim.author: Michael Flynn
eifelheim.why: A physicist and a medieval priest link across centuries around visiting aliens; a rarely mentioned, well-loved book.

mist.title: The Mist
mist.author: Ragnar Jónasson
mist.why: A lonely farm couple in Iceland face a mystery with a twist that left readers stunned; hard to put down.

audition.title: Audition
audition.author: Katie M. Kitamura
audition.why: The comments refer to books by Ryu Murakami and Pip Adam, not this entry; the match is wrong.

return of the king.title: The Return of the King
return of the king.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
return of the king.why: Only mentioned as something someone is listening to; no recommendation in the comments.

harrison bergeron.title: Harrison Bergeron
harrison bergeron.author: Kurt Vonnegut
harrison bergeron.why: Vonnegut's short story of forced equality and handicaps; readers say it stays with them for decades.

paladins grace.title: Paladin's Grace
paladins grace.author: T. Kingfisher
paladins grace.why: A paladin and a perfume maker end up on the run in a funny, warm fantasy romance with a cult following.

we were liars.title: We Were Liars
we were liars.author: E. Lockhart
we were liars.why: Readers split and one found it irritating; not clearly recommended.

fox.title: Fox
fox.author: Joyce Carol Oates
fox.why: Oates's multi-voiced novel with a menacing teacher; readers warn it contains difficult content.

aeneid.title: Aeneid
aeneid.author: Virgil
aeneid.why: Virgil's epic of Aeneas and the founding of Rome; readers suggest Fagles's translation.

vanished birds.title: The vanished birds
vanished birds.author: Simon Jimenez
vanished birds.why: A pilot, a boy and a pull of time across space; lyrical enough to win over readers who dislike science fiction.

powerless.title: Powerless
powerless.author: Lauren Roberts
powerless.why: Readers call it terrible or say they could not get through it; it is not recommended.

matter.title: Matter
matter.author: Iain Banks
matter.why: Banks's Culture novel about a huge ancient artifact and a royal family's war; has a lot of what the poster wanted.

kindly ones.title: The kindly ones
kindly ones.author: Jonathan Littell
kindly ones.why: A French-German SS officer narrates his war in this huge, disturbing novel; recommended for non-horror readers who want shocks.

creation lake.title: Creation Lake
creation lake.author: Rachel Kushner
creation lake.why: Readers split between liking it and calling it pointless; not clearly recommended.

river has roots.title: The River Has Roots
river has roots.author: Amal El-Mohtar
river has roots.why: A short fairytale-like fantasy about two sisters and a willow tree; a read for one afternoon.

feather thief.title: The Feather Thief
feather thief.author: Kirk Wallace Johnson
feather thief.why: A true story of a museum feather heist and its fly-tying obsessive; reads like a caper.

skyward.title: Skyward
skyward.author: Brandon Sanderson
skyward.why: A girl dreams of becoming a starfighter pilot; an energetic YA novel that readers say fits the brief.

lights out.title: Lights Out
lights out.author: Navessa Allen
lights out.why: Readers describe it as horrendous or unfinishable; not recommended.

look to windward.title: Look to windward
look to windward.author: Iain Banks
look to windward.why: Mentioned only in passing as a lesser example; no clear recommendation.

measure.title: The Measure
measure.author: Nikki Erlick
measure.why: Everyone receives a box showing the length of their life; a popular, moving what-if story.

dead zone.title: The Dead Zone
dead zone.author: Stephen King
dead zone.why: A man wakes from a coma with psychic powers; readers say it hooked them without knowing anything about it.

door.title: The Door
door.author: Magda Szabó
door.why: A writer and her formidable housekeeper form a complex bond in Hungary; praised as a deep, moving translated novel.

round house.title: The Round House
round house.author: Louise Erdrich
round house.why: A teenage boy investigates the assault on his mother on a North Dakota reservation; a gripping, powerful Erdrich novel.
